comparisons.title: LangChain vs. LangGraph
comparisons.summary: LangChain provides model, prompt, tool, and retriever abstractions (plus create_agent); LangGraph is the lower-level stateful orchestration runtime powering durable graphs, loops, persistence, and human-in-the-loop interrupts.

rows.left: Standard model/tool/retriever interfaces and high-level agent harness
rows.right: Explicit state machine (nodes, edges, reducers) for durable execution

rows.left: Linear chains or managed create_agent loop
rows.right: Explicit branching, cycles, retries, and deterministic Python routing

rows.left: Message history or short-lived chain inputs
rows.right: Typed state channels with built-in checkpointers across pauses

rows.left: Requires middleware or custom callbacks
rows.right: First-class interrupt() + Command(resume=...) checkpoints

comparisons.whenToChooseLeft: When you need portable chat model wrappers, structured output helpers, or a simple sequential pipeline without complex state pauses.
comparisons.whenToChooseRight: When a workflow needs explicit branching, loops with guardrails, durable checkpointing, or pausing for human approval before external actions.

comparisons.title: Pydantic Models vs. Ordinary Dictionaries
comparisons.summary: Python dictionaries accept any keys and types at runtime without complaint; Pydantic validates, coerces, documents, and exports JSON Schema at runtime.

rows.left: Enforces types, constraints, and custom validators immediately
rows.right: No validation; KeyError or wrong types fail later downstream

rows.left: Generates OpenAPI & JSON Schema automatically
rows.right: Invisible structure; must be documented manually

rows.left: Recursively validates nested models and lists
rows.right: Requires tedious manual isinstance checks everywhere

rows.left: Catches missing/invalid fields with structured ValidationError
rows.right: Silent bugs when an LLM renames or drops a key

comparisons.whenToChooseLeft: At every API boundary, webhook payload, config object, and LLM structured-output parser.
comparisons.whenToChooseRight: For tiny internal scratch maps or dynamic arbitrary key-value bags inside a tightly scoped function.

comparisons.title: Workflow vs. Agent
comparisons.summary: A workflow executes a known sequence of steps defined by the engineer; an agent lets an LLM dynamically choose which tools to call and in what order.

rows.left: Your code / workflow graph (predictable path)
rows.right: The LLM at runtime based on observations

rows.left: Predictable, bounded, usually faster and cheaper
rows.right: Variable; extra reasoning loops add tokens and seconds

rows.left: High; easy to unit test and replay step by step
rows.right: Harder; requires loop limits, tool validation, and evals

rows.left: Support ticket intake, extraction, structured routing
rows.right: Open-ended research where required tool sequence varies per query

comparisons.whenToChooseLeft: Whenever the process steps are known ahead of time (which covers 80%+ of business automations).
comparisons.whenToChooseRight: Only when the path cannot be predetermined and the task genuinely benefits from iterative tool exploration inside strict guardrails.

comparisons.title: Localhost vs. Public Host
comparisons.summary: Localhost always refers to the exact machine or container executing the code right now—not your laptop as seen from the cloud, and not a sibling Docker container.

rows.left: Only processes inside the same OS/container network namespace
rows.right: Reachable across the internet via DNS + public IP or tunnel

rows.left: Private to that host by default
rows.right: Exposed to scanners and bots; requires HTTPS, auth, and firewalling

rows.left: 127.0.0.1 inside n8n container points to n8n itself, not FastAPI!
rows.right: Service names on a shared Docker network or public DNS resolve across hosts

rows.left: External SaaS providers cannot reach http://localhost
rows.right: External webhooks require an HTTPS public endpoint or tunnel

comparisons.whenToChooseLeft: During local development on your own machine when caller and server share the same host OS.
comparisons.whenToChooseRight: When external SaaS webhooks, remote collaborators, or n8n Cloud must reach your FastAPI service.

comparisons.title: HTTP vs. HTTPS
comparisons.summary: HTTP defines request/response semantics in plaintext; HTTPS wraps HTTP inside TLS encryption and server identity verification.

rows.left: Headers, bearer tokens, and bodies travel unencrypted
rows.right: Encrypted end-to-end between client and TLS terminator

rows.left: No cryptographic proof you are talking to the real server
rows.right: TLS certificate proves domain ownership via trusted CA

rows.left: Intermediaries on the path can read or tamper with payloads
rows.right: Tampering breaks TLS MAC verification and fails immediately

rows.left: Rejected by almost all production webhook providers (Slack, Stripe, Telegram)
rows.right: Required standard for all public APIs and webhook endpoints

comparisons.whenToChooseLeft: Strictly inside isolated localhost testing or behind a trusted private VPC/container network after TLS termination.
comparisons.whenToChooseRight: For every public endpoint, API credential exchange, webhook receiver, and client-facing app.

comparisons.title: Webhook vs. Polling
comparisons.summary: Webhooks push an HTTP request to your endpoint the moment an event happens; polling checks an API repeatedly on a timer.

rows.left: Near real-time (seconds after event occurs)
rows.right: Bounded by polling interval (e.g. every 1-15 minutes)

rows.left: Requires a reachable HTTPS URL and signature verification
rows.right: Needs only outbound HTTP requests; works behind NAT/firewalls

rows.left: If endpoint is down during retries, events can be dropped
rows.right: Can resume from last cursor/timestamp after downtime

rows.left: Zero wasted calls when nothing changes
rows.right: Uses rate-limit budget even when inbox is empty

comparisons.whenToChooseLeft: When the source system supports reliable signed webhooks and you want immediate event processing.
comparisons.whenToChooseRight: When the source lacks webhooks, sits behind a firewall without inbound access, or needs a periodic reconciliation sweep.

comparisons.title: RAG vs. Fine-Tuning
comparisons.summary: RAG injects fresh, permission-filtered facts into the prompt at query time; fine-tuning updates model weights offline to teach style, format, or specialized task patterns.

rows.left: Updates immediately when docs change or are deleted
rows.right: Frozen at training time; requires retraining to update facts

rows.left: Can filter retrieved chunks per user/tenant at runtime
rows.right: Memorized weights cannot enforce per-user document ACLs

rows.left: Can cite exact document IDs and snippets retrieved
rows.right: Cannot reliably cite which training row produced a claim

rows.left: Help docs, company policies, ticket history, changing catalogs
rows.right: Teaching consistent tone, compact domain classification, or latency optimization

comparisons.whenToChooseLeft: Whenever answers depend on changing facts, company policies, citations, or user permissions.
comparisons.whenToChooseRight: When you already have a clean, curated dataset and need consistent format, domain tone, or smaller-model performance.

comparisons.title: Cloudflare Tunnel vs. Hosting
comparisons.summary: Hosting runs your FastAPI/n8n processes on compute with CPU, RAM, and disk; Cloudflare Tunnel only creates a secure outbound bridge from where your app already runs to Cloudflare's edge.

rows.left: No — cloudflared forwards traffic to a server running elsewhere
rows.right: Yes — provides the compute, RAM, and runtime for your containers

rows.left: Not needed; establishes outbound encrypted connections
rows.right: Usually requires firewall rules (80/443) unless paired with Tunnel

rows.left: Connectivity layer only — NOT application authentication
rows.right: Your app (plus Access/proxy) enforces auth and authorization

rows.left: If your local machine sleeps or shuts down, tunnel returns 502/530
rows.right: Cloud VPS/PaaS stays online 24/7 independent of your laptop

comparisons.whenToChooseLeft: To safely expose a self-hosted homelab/VPC service without opening inbound firewall ports (paired with Access/app auth).
comparisons.whenToChooseRight: Always required somewhere to actually execute your FastAPI, database, and n8n processes reliably 24/7.

comparisons.title: n8n Orchestration vs. Python Backend Service
comparisons.summary: n8n excels at visual SaaS integrations, OAuth connectors, schedules, and webhook triggers; Python excels at complex data contracts, testing, AI logic, and versioned code.

rows.left: Hundreds of built-in OAuth triggers and app nodes
rows.right: Must write and maintain SDK/HTTP client glue manually

rows.left: Hard to unit test complex branching visually
rows.right: First-class pytest unit/integration/eval suites in CI

rows.left: Basic expressions/IF nodes become brittle at scale
rows.right: Pydantic BaseModels guarantee strict runtime contracts

rows.left: Large JSON exports are noisy to diff and review
rows.right: Clean modular Python diffs, PR reviews, and linters

comparisons.whenToChooseLeft: For triggers (Gmail/Webhook/Slack), CRM connectors, human-notification routing, and non-fragile SaaS glue.
comparisons.whenToChooseRight: For Pydantic validation, LLM calls, RAG pipelines, LangGraph state machines, complex loops, and automated evals.

comparisons.title: Authentication (AuthN) vs. Authorization (AuthZ)
comparisons.summary: Authentication verifies identity (API key, JWT, user session); Authorization checks whether that verified identity is allowed to access a specific resource or action.

rows.left: Is this caller really Service A or User Alice?
rows.right: May Alice read Tenant B's support tickets or issue refunds?

rows.left: 401 Unauthorized (missing or invalid credentials)
rows.right: 403 Forbidden (valid identity, insufficient permission)

rows.left: Validating bearer token on /v1/search
rows.right: Filtering vector search chunks by user's tenant_id and role

rows.left: Trusting an unverified X-User-Id header
rows.right: Checking login once at gateway but forgetting row-level tenant checks

comparisons.whenToChooseLeft: First step on every protected endpoint, webhook receiver, or internal microservice call.
comparisons.whenToChooseRight: On every data query, RAG retrieval filter, and high-impact tool call (refunds, deletions, sends).
